text: Four thousand, four hundred forty-five dollars. Five lines on a hospital bill, and nothing tells you what any of them should cost.
This is BillCheck. Paste the bill, and an AI reads each line. Code checks every number against the bill itself.
Then each line it can price meets its twenty twenty-six Medicare rate.
The emergency visit: twenty-four hundred billed. Medicare pays four twenty-six. Private plans paid, on average, two point seven nine times that. So the negotiation reference is eleven eighty-nine.
The CT scan: sixteen fifty billed, two ninety-eight as a reference.
The blood tests are usually included in the visit payment, and the injection has no confirmed benchmark. BillCheck says so, instead of guessing.
What's left adds up to one thousand, eight hundred eighty-two dollars and thirty-eight cents.
That amount goes straight into PayPal's sandbox checkout. The server sets it; the browser never can.
Payment captured. BillCheck then issues an itemized invoice at the suggested amounts, from the provider's sandbox account, and marks it paid with this same payment.
One bill. One number you can pay. And every rule signed by a physician.
